server.name: soundcheck
server.title: Soundcheck — Live Event Staffing
server.description: Staff live events: gigs, crew, setlists, call lists, ingest. Hosted MCP with OAuth.

protocolMetadata.instructions: Soundcheck runs live events: gigs, crew staffing (offers, invitations, availability), call lists, setlists, venues, customers, sponsors, leads, inventory, the org mailbox, imports and gig-file ingestion. Tools act as the signed-in user in their organization; coordinator actions need an org role. Read tools are safe to call freely. Preview first and get the user's OK before tools that message real people (send_message, broadcast_event_reminder, send_reminder, invite_org_member, invite_customer_contact_to_portal, create_form_assignment with notify_customer, update_event when it moves a gig's dates, times or location) or write imported or ingested data (commit_import, import_file, commit_ingestion_file, commit_ingestion_batch). Call get_org_agent_profile at session start; search_org_knowledge recalls venue quirks, past incidents and lost-lead reasons (guidance only; facts and money come from the other tools). Turn a client brief into a draft gig with create_event_plan → update_event_plan → review_event_plan → create_draft_event_from_plan. Use search_soundcheck_docs to learn how a feature works before guessing, and get_soundcheck_link to send the user to the web app for visual review or work this server does not do (new contracts, billing, payouts, integrations, branding). Deletes, archives, sends and other destructive or outbound writes are confirmation-gated: the first call returns status confirmation_required with a confirmation_token and does not write. Show the summary, get approval, then repeat the call with the same arguments plus confirmation_token.

tool.name: list_events
tool.title: List events
tool.description: List events visible to the authenticated user. Filter by organization, user, or status. Paginated with limit (max 100) and offset. Each row is a nested envelope {event, assignments, members, invitations}: the gig's id, title, date and event_status live on row.event, not on the row itself — match a gig by row.event.title. event_status is an exact match: an unarchived gig is UNARCHIVED, not ACTIVE, so omit the filter (or pass UNARCHIVED) to find one. event_status="TEMPLATE" lists the organization's gig templates — the ones create_event_plan and suggest_plan_templates plan from. The onboarding sample gig (row.event.is_sample=true) is left out unless include_sample is true. event_status="DELETED" instead lists gigs deleted in the last 30 days that restore_event can bring back: flat rows with deleted_by and deletion_scheduled_for, gig managers only, organization_id defaults to your active org, no pagination.

tool.name: list_event_chat_messages
tool.title: List event chat messages
tool.description: List Soundcheck-stored messages for an event group chat (the webhook-persisted store, not live Twilio history), or pass message_id to get that one message. Each row includes citation_id (stable; same as id), citation_body_hash, citation_version, status (SENT | EDITED | DELETED), edited_at / deleted_at, author identity/display name/user id, channel (CHAT | SMS), created_provider_timestamp (immutable pagination order; page with before set to the last returned id), provider_timestamp, and media metadata. Cite with citation_id plus hash/version — do not treat a DELETED or superseded body as current. Chat members and gig managers only. Uses the authenticated user Clerk backend auth; never mints or returns a Twilio token.

tool.name: get_attention_items
tool.title: Get attention items
tool.description: List what needs an org owner's or admin's attention on upcoming gigs (next 30 days): deterministic findings where something changed and is still unfinished — call times changed after crew were notified, crew dropped off with shifts still open, a guest-count change with open tasks, billing terms changed with an unpaid receivable, or staffing short close to the gig. Each item has a classification (BLOCKING, NEEDS_ATTENTION, WATCH, FYI), a deterministic `reason`, the gig, affected people/records, and `evidence` records (kind + id + summary + timestamp) to cite as provenance, plus a navigation-only `suggested_action`. Sorted most urgent first. Owner/admin only; defaults to your active org. Read-only — resolve anything through the existing confirm-gated tools.

tool.name: create_event
tool.title: Create event
tool.description: Create a new event in an organization. By default the event is ACTIVE (published) as soon as it is created: crew can see it, and invitations added to it go out normally. Pass draft=true to create it as a DRAFT instead, as the web and mobile apps do: a draft is hidden from crew and holds its invitations until someone publishes it in the web app (MCP cannot publish). Ask the user which they want when it is unclear. The authenticated user is added as a member by default (pass member_ids to override, including [] to skip). For a multi-day gig pass end_date (YYYY-MM-DD, after event_date) and no start_time or end_time: a multi-day gig carries dates only, and passing times with one is refused. Per-day times belong in the run of show or on each shift. start_time and end_time are for single-day gigs and optional. Returns the new event id and resolved members.

tool.name: update_event
tool.title: Update event
tool.description: Update only the event fields you provide; an omitted field is left as stored. title takes precedence over its name alias; empty notes or location clears that field. end_date (YYYY-MM-DD) is the last day of a multi-day gig and must be on or after event_date; pass end_date: null to make the gig single-day again. start_time and end_time apply to single-day gigs. A multi-day gig carries dates only: setting times on one is refused (set per-day times in the run of show or on each shift), and an older multi-day gig that still has times can only have them cleared with start_time: null and end_time: null (clearing either clears both). Extending a timed single-day gig with end_date clears its times automatically. Whenever times are cleared that way, crew shifts that inherited them keep them as their own call times, and an empty run of show gets one section per day starting at the old start time. When event_date or end_date moves and no times are given, any stored local clock times move with it. Shortening the range onto days that still have accepted or pending crew is refused with the affected days named; resolve those crew first or finish in the web app. Confirmation-gated when the call sets or clears event_date, end_date, start_time or end_time, or sets a non-empty location, because the API then sends the gig's invited crew a schedule-change notification: the first call writes nothing and returns confirmation_required with a summary; show it to the user and, once they approve, resend the same arguments plus confirmation_token. Edits to only title, name, notes, or clearing location with an empty string are not gated. Concurrent edits to different fields are preserved; edits to the same field are last-write-wins. Use dedicated event lifecycle tools to change status.

end_date.description: optional last day of a multi-day gig as YYYY-MM-DD, on or after event_date; null clears it (single-day gig); omit to leave unchanged

end_time.description: optional new end time of a single-day gig (RFC3339 with numeric UTC offset, or unix epoch seconds); null clears it; omit to leave unchanged; refused on a multi-day gig

event_date.description: optional new first day of the gig (YYYY-MM-DD, RFC3339 string or unix epoch seconds); cannot be cleared

start_time.description: optional new start time of a single-day gig (RFC3339 with numeric UTC offset, or unix epoch seconds); null clears it; omit to leave unchanged; refused on a multi-day gig

guest_count.description: optional estimated guest count; null clears it; stored on the gig, not in notes

tool.name: apply_calllist_to_event
tool.title: Apply call list to event
tool.description: Drop a call list onto a gig as DRAFT shifts (mode=draft_shifts, the default): one draft shift per position slot, covering every day of the gig, sized at max(seats, assigned members), with the people penciled into the template attached as un-sent draft recipients. NOTHING IS SENT AND NOBODY IS NOTIFIED — the admin reviews the roster and sets fees, then sends the offers. Re-applying is a no-op for slots this template already put on the gig (DRAFT/OPEN/FILLED); withdrawn or expired shifts leave a hole a re-apply refills. Both modes also add each template labor call line whose department the gig does not already have (case-insensitive) to the gig labor call, which writes its house labor shifts; labor_departments_added counts them. Returns shifts_created / recipients_added / skipped, plus a `hint` explaining why when 0 shifts were created (no org positions, template members without a position, empty slots, or already applied). mode=event_members is the legacy path: it adds roster rows instead of shifts, primaries (call_order 0) INVITED and backups STANDBY, and puts nothing on the Staffing board. Either mode commits people from the template onto a real gig, so it is confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set.

mode.description: draft_shifts (default) creates draft shifts; event_members is the legacy roster path

event_id.description: the event to apply the calllist to

tool.name: import_event_from_url

tool.description: Save an event link as a gig. A new link creates a DRAFT gig; a link imported before updates that same gig and keeps its status. Pass the event fields from preview_event_from_url, edited as the user asked, and only the preview sections the user kept: run_of_show is written to the gig run of show, venue is linked, organizer becomes a show contact, requirements become tasks, links become gig links (with the event page), image_url becomes the gig cover, capacity fills an empty guest count, suggested_gig_type sets the gig type. title and event_date are required.

tool.name: create_event_invitations
tool.title: Create event invitations
tool.description: Invite people to a specific gig (event-scoped — NOT org membership; use invite_org_member for that). Each invitation names an org member by user_id (IN_APP) or an external person by email (EMAIL) or phone_number (SMS), optionally with org_position_id from list_org_positions, call_order (0 primary, 1+ backup), and a performance_fee. On an ACTIVE gig the person is notified immediately by email/SMS/push by default; pass send_invitation=false to store unsent drafts and send them later with send_event_invitations. On a DRAFT gig every invitation is held unsent until the gig is published with publish_event or the Soundcheck app, whatever send_invitation says, so do not tell the user anyone was notified. Gig coordinators may only invite existing members by user_id. Pass invitations:[{"email":"sam@example.com"}] (or the emails:["sam@example.com"] shorthand); this tool is event-scoped and takes no organization_id. Writes to real people, so it is confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set. Verify with list_event_invitations.

tool.description: Send a gig's unsent (draft) invitations — the ones created with send_invitation=false — by email/SMS/push. tool.name: send_crew_offer
tool.title: Send crew offer (shift)
tool.description: Send a shift to crew: flips a DRAFT to OPEN and notifies recipients by email/SMS/push. Omit recipient_ids/recipients to send to the recipients already attached (or the linked call list); pass them to add or target specific people. recipients[] carries per-person fees for people this send ADDS and its user_ids are sent too (no need to repeat them in recipient_ids); a fee for someone already attached is refused here — set it with update_crew_offer first. The confirmation token binds the exact people who will be notified (named plus already attached) and their fees, so attaching someone or changing a fee after approval re-gates the send. Re-sending an OPEN shift reaches newly added people and attached PENDING recipients whose delivery status is NOT_SENT (the tool refuses a no-op send and says so); use send_reminder kind=crew_offer for nudges. To ask someone who declined again, name them in recipient_ids and pass reask_dates with the day or days to re-ask. With no recipients given, the current members of the linked call list are resolved now and sent by id. Messages real people, so it is confirmation-gated when MCP_CONFIRMATION_SECRET is set — the confirmation summary names the shift and who will be notified.

offer_id.description: crew offer id from list_crew_offers / create_crew_offer

fee.description: fee for this person, overriding the offer fee

reask_dates.description: YYYY-MM-DD days to ask the people in recipient_ids again after they declined them (one day or several). Their declined days on those dates go back to pending and they are notified. Days that have passed stay declined. Without this, a send never re-asks someone who declined.

confirmation_token.description: leave empty on the first call; the server returns confirmation_required + a token, then resend the SAME args with that token to proceed

tool.description: Add a line to a gig's finances, as the GUI Finances tab does: ledger_type INCOME (money received), RECEIVABLE (an invoice/what a client owes), EXPENSE (money spent), or PAYABLE (a cost or payout still owed — set counterparty_user_id or counterparty_name). amount is positive in the item's currency (default USD); date is the civil day YYYY-MM-DD. account_id is resolved automatically when the org has one account of the matching type; otherwise pick one from list_ledger_accounts. tool.name: enrich_venue
tool.title: Research venue details
tool.description: Research a venue on the web (via context.dev) and return a PROPOSAL of venue details and stages: capacity, venue type, stage size, load-in/out, dock, elevator, parking, wifi, dressing rooms, green room, house tech, amenities, restrictions, published booking contact, plus the stages or rooms the venue books separately. Each value carries a source_url and a short evidence excerpt. NOTHING is written. Show the proposal to the user, and only after they confirm apply what they choose with update_venue (venue fields) and save_venue_stage (stages, including stage_size and house_tech). The same venue is cached for 24 hours and each organization has a daily limit. Returns 503 ENRICHMENT_UNAVAILABLE when research is not configured, and 422 VENUE_IDENTITY_MISSING when the venue has neither an address nor a website.

tool.name: get_event_labor_call
tool.title: Get gig labor call
tool.description: Get a gig's local labor call: the stagehand order placed with the venue or union (e.g. IATSE), one row per department with a call time and a headcount of hands for load-in, show and load-out. Hands are counts, not named crew — for named crew use the staffing tools. Call times are HH:MM wall clocks in the gig's timezone. Returns the whole labor call: union_local, steward, steward_call, head_electrician, head_electrician_call, notes, departments (id, department, load_in_call, load_in_hands, show_call, show_hands, load_out_call, load_out_hands, load_out_next_day, notes, sort_order) and totals (load_in_hands, show_hands, load_out_hands). Each department phase with hands or a call is a house labor shift on the gig's Staffing board: load-in on the first day, show every day, load-out on the last day. A load-out call earlier than the show call (or the load-in call, or 06:00 when neither is set) falls on the next morning and load_out_next_day is true. Anyone on the gig can read it.

tool.name: update_event_plan

tool.description: Apply edits to a plan: answer or dismiss its questions, set a field, choose between competing candidates, resolve the venue/customer match, edit schedule entries and anchors, adjust staffing roles, edit checklist tasks, acknowledge a conflict, or switch template. Send the user's own answers — never infer or default a year, date, timezone, budget, headcount, venue, or client the brief does not state. When a field has more than one candidate, show every candidate to the user and let them choose. dry_run=true previews the effect (including how anchored schedule entries move) and writes nothing. operations.description: edits to apply, in order, each an object with an "op" discriminant and flat fields (never a nested "entry"/"role"/"task" object). Value edits: {op:"set_value", path, value} and {op:"answer_question", question_id, value} / {op:"dismiss_question", question_id}. Ambiguity: {op:"choose_candidate", path, candidate_index} and {op:"resolve_record", kind:"venue"|"customer", resolution:"matched"|"none"|"create_later", record_id?, record_name?}. Use it to hand off: (1) visual review — a gig, its staffing board, finances, or a plan; (2) work this server does not do — sending a new contract (PDF upload), billing and payouts, integrations, email domains, branding, or deleting the organization. Share the returned url with the user as a link. Targets: event = one gig (event_id); events = the gigs list; event_plan = one gig plan (plan_id); venue = one venue; venues = the venues list; customer = one customer; customers = the customers list; person = one person (user_id); people = the crew / people list; setlist = one setlist; run_of_show = one run-of-show template; import = one import job; availability = availability; crew_offers = crew offers board; crew_members = crew (non-staff) members and their removal; opens the Crew workspace when the org has it, otherwise the full member roster; leads = the leads pipeline; sponsors = sponsors; inventory = inventory; offerings = the offering catalog; finances = org finances; inbox = the org mailbox; org_members = org staff and members, roles, and removal (staff only when the org has the Crew workspace; use crew_members for crew); org_positions = org crew positions; org_billing = plan and billing; org_payments = payout and payment settings; org_integrations = integrations (connect / disconnect); org_email = email sending domains; org_profile = organization name, logo, timezone, public profile, and deletion. Read-only; no data is fetched, so pass ids you already have.

tool.name: send_feedback
tool.title: Send feedback to Soundcheck
tool.description: Send feedback to the people who build this product (not the user's organization, crew, or clients). It carries bug reports, feature suggestions, support questions, and praise, plus problems with these tools that the user agreed to report, and contains only what the user asked or agreed to send. It creates a Linear issue for the product team (email fallback if Linear is unavailable); it does not message anyone in the user's organization (the messaging tools do that). The team replies to the user's account email when there is something to answer.

Takes no arguments. Use open_gig for one gig's detail view. Read-only.

tool.name: read_integration_data

tool.description: Read live data from one of the organization's connected integrations, for example open QuickBooks invoices, HubSpot deals, Flex inventory, files in a Google Drive folder, or messages in a gig's Slack channel. _published_faq.name: How do I add Soundcheck — Live Event Staffing to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Soundcheck — Live Event Staffing to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.soundchecklive.io/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is Soundcheck — Live Event Staffing MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, Soundcheck — Live Event Staffing scores 100/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Soundcheck — Live Event Staffing's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, Soundcheck — Live Event Staffing scores 84/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 253 of 253 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Soundcheck — Live Event Staffing?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Soundcheck — Live Event Staffing in productivity on the Manufact MCP catalog include Autodesk Product Help, BoardWise, FlagStat, Keenable Web Search, and PomoDial.

_published_faq.name: How can Soundcheck — Live Event Staffing improve its MCP documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: list_event_links is the lowest-scoring reviewed tool at 66/100. Describe the returned fields so an agent can interpret the result. Open its review for feedback and a copyable fix prompt, then rerun the documentation review after updating your tool metadata.
